title: The Hall of the Scales
text: A jackal-headed judge waits beside a golden scale and a single white feather. Behind him something large breathes in the dark. He will weigh each heart, he says, and give back the light ones lighter still. He does not say what he does with the heavy ones.

options.label: Kneel, and let him weigh your hearts against the feather.

outcomes.text: Each of you steps onto the scale. You come down lighter, and a little emptier, and the thing in the dark breathes slower, satisfied.

options.label: Refuse the scale. Your hearts are not his to weigh.

outcomes.text: He rises from beside his scale, and the thing breathing in the dark behind him rises too, and it is hungry.

options.label: Put a thumb on the scale while the judge looks away, and hope he never looks back.

outcomes.text: The Leader's thumb tips the balance. The judge sees it, and says nothing, and stands. His silence is worse than anger.
The thumb slips. The heart is weighed heavy, and something in the dark is fed. Then the judge stands.
